why: The statement is a bare title; following the record, the core question is the discrete symmetric problem (optimal expected meeting time for each n). Line, sphere, cube, labelled-deterministic and restricted-strategy results are variants. The key close call is Cembrano–Fischer–Klimm: it answers negatively whether Anderson–Weber is optimal for n ≥ 4, but the statement names no such sub-question, and what the result does to the problem's quantity is lower the best-known upper bound on the optimal value for every n ≥ 4 while leaving the optimum open, so it is a bound (F4), not a case. The explicit FSD strategy is a record construction, not a counterexample to anything the statement asserts, so object_role is null. Pre-snapshot n = 2 (1990) and n = 3 (Weber 2009, MOR 2012) are journal-accepted cases; Weber's K4 note and the Dani et al. and Bonamy et al. lower bounds are bounds. Georgiou et al.'s ChatGPT use (exploratory discussion, code generation, debugging, consistency checks) credits it with no stated mathematics in the result, so none, and the event is a variant anyway.
doubts: Cembrano et al.'s AI statement and acknowledgements were unread, so its ai_role of none is conditional. Its n = 4 formula comes only from a fetch summary. If the bullet were read as asking specifically whether Anderson–Weber is optimal, Cembrano et al. would be a case (or whole for n ≥ 4) rather than a bound. Several journal acceptances (Alpern–Gal, Ta-Shma–Zwick, Dani et al.) are known only from snippets.
